item.title: 😎 Bayern Munich hit six and go top of the Bundesliga
item.description: 😎 Bayern Munich hit six and go top of the Bundesliga Bayern Munich thrashed RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday (17) to go top of the Bundesliga. Luis Díaz (three), Pavlovic, Olise and Harry Kane scored the goals at the Allianz Arena. Highlights coming soon. Bayern moved up to 14 points, overtaking Borussia Dortmund, who also have 14 points but an inferior goal difference. To stay top, however, Bayern will have to hope Freiburg slip up. Freiburg have 13 points and visit Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday (18). And the next round of Bundesliga fixtures will see Freiburg face Bayern Munich on Sunday the 25th at 1:30 p.m. Before that, Bayern will turn their attention to the Champions League. They host Arsenal in a blockbuster clash at 4 p.m. on Wednesday (21). How Bayern vs RB Leipzig unfolded Bayern Munich opened the scoring in the 12th minute. Luis Díaz latched onto Kimmich's ball in behind the defence and finished in style: 1-0. Díaz then turned provider, finding Pavlovic in the box to double the lead. Still in the first half, Olise made it 3-0 with an assist from Harry Kane. Bayern kept up the tempo, turning the win into a rout in the second half. Díaz scored twice more, and Harry Kane got on the scoresheet. Maksimovic scored a fine consolation goal for RB Leipzig in stoppage time. item.title: Rangers Midfielder Wanted Again By Beşiktaş: Should McInnes Sell Him In January?
item.description: Rangers Midfielder Wanted Again By Beşiktaş: Should McInnes Sell Him In January? Four times now. That’s how often a Turkish giant has come knocking for one of Derek McInnes ‘s most prized midfielders, and four times the move has fallen apart. Takvim, relayed via Sport Witness , says Beşiktaş still haven’t given up. The Istanbul club plans to return in January, and they’re casting the net wider this time, with West Ham defender Konstantinos Mavropanos also sitting on their shortlist. Nicolas Raskin is the man at the heart of it. The 25-year-old Belgian international arrived from Standard Liège in January 2023 for a modest fee and has since become the engine of the Ibrox midfield. His contract runs until 2028, and a €15m price tag keeps cropping up in the chatter. How close did Raskin come to leaving? Closer than most fans realised. Late in the summer window, reports claimed Beşiktaş had a deal sorted, and Raskin appeared set to fly out. Then he turned up in the squad for the Falkirk game, played 90 minutes and rejected the offer. He admitted afterwards he’d been mentally ready to go, yet he also called the matter closed. That door hasn’t slammed shut for good, though. Should McInnes sell Raskin in January? GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – OCTOBER 10: Nicolas Raskin of Rangers is seen warming up during the William Hill Premiership 2026/27 match between Glasgow Rangers and Kilmarnock at Ibrox Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) If I’m McInnes, I say no unless the money’s silly. Raskin is the one midfielder I can’t easily replace. He carries the ball out of tight spaces, he wins second balls, and he already knows exactly what I want from him. Selling midseason means hunting for a like-for-like option while rival clubs charge a premium for desperation. That rarely ends well. Then there’s the head issue. Raskin has said he was ready to leave, and a player with one foot out of the door can drift. I’d sit him down, tell him straight what the plan is, and watch his training closely. If his standards slip, the decision makes itself. The €15m figure isn’t bad for a player who cost a modest fee, yet it’s no fortune either. A bigger league might offer more come summer, and Beşiktaş can’t match that stage. I’d tell the board to hold firm and only talk if a Premier League or Serie A club turns up. Otherwise, he stays, and I keep the engine running.

item.title: Unstoppable Kai Rooney scores just 24 hours after emotional U21s debut
item.description: Unstoppable Kai Rooney scores just 24 hours after emotional U21s debut Manchester United U18s took on Nottingham Forest U18s in league action on Saturday afternoon. A repeat of the U21s fixture the night before, United looked to exact some revenge after the U21s dramatically dropped points for the first time this season. Kai Rooney made his U21s debut on Friday night and, less than 24 hours later, was named in Darren Fletcher’s starting XI for the U18s as the manager made five changes from last week’s Premier League Cup clash with Chelsea. First half United threatened early on, with a Junior Brown effort flying narrowly wide of the target in the fifth minute. The young Red Devils played on the front foot and their high press reaped the reward when the Forest keeper, Alastair Graham, had his pass blocked by Emmanuel Ziro, allowing Rooney to pounce and tuck the ball into the net from close range for his first goal of the season. Rooney thought he had his second of the game in the 20th minute when he rounded Graham and finished into an open net, but the assistant’s flag spoiled his celebrations with an offside call. Jay McEvoy then looked to get his name on the scoresheet, forcing quick reflexes from Graham to keep out the midfielder’s effort. The opening 45 minutes was all one-way action, but the score remained 0-1 at the break, with Graham doing well to keep out late efforts from Brown and Rooney. Second half Brown and Rooney combined early in the second half when Rooney came close to scoring off the rebound from Brown’s shot, but an important block off the line by the defender kept United’s lead at just one. Last night’s match winner in the U21s fixture, Shakur Samuels, forced Charlie Hardy into action for the first time in the match with a low, driven effort. Brown enjoyed a fruitful game down the wing as he consistently opened up Forest, but was unable to take advantage as his shot sailed narrowly wide of the post again. Against the run of play, Forest drew the match level in the 78th minute. A brotherly connection provided the blow: Jubilee Ntege’s cross was taken down by his brother, Rabbi Ntege, and finished with a dipping shot past Hardy. Despite finishing with 76% of possession, United were unable to turn their dominance into a winner, as late attempts from Jariyah Shah and McEvoy were unable to beat the keeper. The draw leaves United in third place, with a big clash to come next Saturday against Liverpool. Match facts United: Hardy; Shah, McCormack (c), Ngwashi (Emsden-James 73), O’Brien (Laurie 88); Carrick (J. Watson 65), Eze (McLaughlin 66); Ziro, McEvoy, Brown; Rooney (D. Nkoto 66). Subs not used: Z. Watson, Silvester. Goals: Rooney 13

item.title: The Real Reason Kane’s Record-Breaking Assist Changed History
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Patrick Kane etched his name into the history books on Thursday night at the United Center. He recorded his 895th career assist, a helper that put Connor Bedard past the Winnipeg Jets net. This single play moved Kane past Phil Housley for the most assists ever by a U.S.-born player in the NHL. The crowd roared as the American legend cemented a legacy that few thought he would still be adding to at this stage of his career. The goal came during a power-play situation where the Blackhawks held a 5-on-3 advantage. Bedard fired the puck home to score his first goal of the 2026-27 season. It was also the first goal of his career while wearing the captain’s “C.” Tyler Bertuzzi also earned an assist on the play, marking his 200th career helper in the league. A New Chapter for Bedard Connor Bedard has been the face of the franchise since he was drafted. He finally broke his goalless streak for the season in a way that mattered most. According to Yahoo Sports , Kane was genuinely impressed with the shot Bedard unleashed. The connection between the veteran star and the young captain seems to be growing stronger every time they step on the ice together. Their chemistry on the top line is becoming a major weapon for the team. Roman Kantserov, a rookie who plays on the same line, watched the moment unfold with awe. He told RG.org that the reception Kane received when he returned to Chicago was unforgettable. “There are legends here, and Kane is back,” Kantserov said. He noted that the crowd’s energy was so loud that television cameras just could not capture the full feeling of the room. For a young player like Kantserov, sharing the ice with Kane is a dream come true. Surpassing Phil Housley is a massive milestone for American hockey. Housley was a dominant force, but Kane’s consistency over nearly two decades is what allowed him to reach the top spot. This record highlights the growth of U.S. talent in a sport that has long been dominated by Canadian and European players. “He’s got the same drive and passion, which I think is going to have a long-lasting effect on a lot of these players inside that dressing room,” Olczyk said. Olczyk added that Kane’s influence on the franchise will last a long time, regardless of how many points he scores from here on. The young players in the locker room see what it takes to stay at the top level for so long. They see the work ethic required to set a record that stood for years. The Road Ahead The Blackhawks now have a captain who has scored his first goal and a legend who has set a new standard. The team faces a tough schedule ahead, but the momentum from this game could be a turning point. Roman Kantserov admitted that he had to prove himself after skipping the AHL to join the big club. Kane and Bedard immediately placed him on the first power-play unit, a move that worked at once, he observed. But for one night in Chicago, the focus was on a number that will stand for a long time: 895.

item.title: Chiefs Must Trade For George Pickens To Fix Their Deep Threat
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0 and humming along, but their passing game has a glaring hole that won’t fix itself. Patrick Mahomes needs a receiver who can stretch the field and win contested catches, and Rashee Rice is out with a hamstring injury for Sunday’s game against the Chargers. According to Yahoo Sports , general manager Brett Veach must target George Pickens before the November 10 trade deadline to give this team its best shot at a fifth ring. The team cannot rely on Xavier Worthy alone to do the heavy lifting downfield. Pickens is the only name on the list who fits the bill for a true difference-maker. Following the failure to secure a long-term extension with the franchise tag in Dallas, his future past the 2026 season remains uncertain as he plays under that designation now. Should the Cowboys drop from contention, trading him may become their sole method to regain draft assets instead of watching him depart in free agency, presenting a difficult decision. While Jerry Jones would probably insist on a significant return, Kansas City might deem the expense justified if they view Pickens as Mahomes’ primary target for the upcoming four or five years. Why A Rental Like Mooney Is Not Enough Some analysts suggest Darnell Mooney makes sense because he is cheap and fits the intermediate zone, but that is a short-term fix for a long-term problem. According to Arrowhead Addict , Mooney is averaging just 3.4 targets and 1.6 catches per game while playing third fiddle to Malik Nabers. He is a rental for a 2027 or 2028 seventh-round pick, which is not sexy and does not solve the lack of a dynamic playmaker. The Chiefs require a player who can alter a game instantly with a single touch, much like Tyreek Hill did during his tenure with the franchise. Jerry Jeudy is another option mentioned by Yahoo Sports, but he would be a different kind of addition who does not necessarily require a massive trade package. Although his route-running skills suit Andy Reid’s offense, he currently occupies a diminished role with the Cleveland Browns. While he could maximize his strengths in space, he lacks the superstar potential that Pickens brings to the table. Improvement does not strictly require a superstar for Kansas City, yet these three prospects possess such potential and deserve Veach’s attention as the deadline nears. item.title: Top-20 matchup between Houston, Oklahoma State is officially a sellout
item.description: Houston Cougars fans cheer during the first half of an NCAA college football game against West Virginia on Thursday, Oct. 12, 2023, in Houston. (Brett Coomer/Staff photographer) The top-20 Big 12 matchup between Houston and Oklahoma State is officially sold out, the school announced Saturday. A crowd of at least 40,000 is expected for Saturday's 6:30 p.m. game, marking the eighth sellout in the 13-year history of TDECU Stadium. "We had a feeling this was possible and knew if we built it the right way, great things would happen," UH athletic director Eddie Nuñez said. "Thank you to the fans, students and everyone coming to the game for making this happen. It It will be UH's first home sellout since 42,806 fans attended the Texas Tech game last season and its third sellout since the school joined the Big 12 in 2023. The 2023 game against Texas drew 42,280 fans, the second-largest crowd in stadium history. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Chicago Bears activate Kyler Gordon, Dayo Odeyingbo to injured reserve
item.description: Oct 6, 2024; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) celebrates after the game against the Carolina Panthers at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Bartel-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Chicago Bears announced several roster moves today, including activating defensive back Kyler Gordon from the Physically Unable to Perform list. Gordon has not played this season while rehabbing a calf injury he suffered in the offseason. He was in the midst of his 21-day practice window and was a full participant for all 9 practices over the last three weeks. At yesterday’s press conference, head coach Ben Johnson said this about Gordon, “He’s done a great job taking everything that we’ve assigned him so far. I feel good about him — whether that’s this week or next week — being able to contribute to this team and help us out, and there’s a number of ways he can do that. But I’m encouraged with what I’ve seen so far.” On Thursday, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen met the media and said this about Gordon, “He’s been working extremely hard. He’s been great around the building. He’s been doing everything we’ve asked him to do. I’ve been impressed with him.” It’ll be interesting to see how the Bears deploy Gordon on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons, because while most of his NFL experience has been at nickel, he’s also played and practiced at corner and safety. His versatility, if he can stay healthy, will provide the Bears’ defense a huge boost. The Bears also signed defensive back Nick McCloud to the 53-man roster from their practice squad, placed defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) on injured reserve, and released safety Xavier Woods. Odeyingbo is second on the team with 3 sacks, third with 3 tackles for loss, and he leads Chicago defensive linemen with 2 batted passes. He’ll miss at least 4 games on IR. Chicago also announced that they’re elevating linebacker Buddy Johnson and running back Zavier Scott from the practice squad for Sunday’s game. They’ll revert to the practice squad after the game.

item.title: Finally finding club form, USMNT star Gio Reyna flourishing with goal against PSG in Ligue 1
item.description: Finally finding club form, USMNT star Gio Reyna flourishing with goal against PSG in Ligue 1 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Gio Reyna has been a regular for the U.S. national team under Mauricio Pochettino since returning to the national team fold in late 2025, but it has not been as smooth sailing for the 23-year-old American at the club level. After struggling for multiple seasons in Germany, first with Borussia Dortmund and then for a year at Borussia Monchengladbach, Reyna has found it difficult to break into either squad and earn a regular starting role. So this season, Reyna dumped the Bundesliga and moved to France, where he joined BlueCo club Strasbourg hoping to turn his club career around. Early signs are promising, as Reyna has slotted into a starting role with the club immediately under Portuguese manager Hugo Oliveria. MORE: All the latest USMNT news Gio Reyna goal vs. PSG In the 14th minute of the Ligue 1 meeting between PSG and Strasbourg on Saturday at Stade de la Meinau, Gio Reyna gave the hosts an early lead as he snuck the ball in at the near post by Matvey Safanov. The move was largely down to Reyna who created the moment for himself, first playing a give-and-go with right-winger Gessime Yassine before charging into the penalty area on the ball and picking out the inside of the near post. The moment was a shock, as PSG were expected to walk the match against their opponents in the bottom half of the Ligue 1 table. Giovanni Reyna goal vs PSG #USMNT https://t.co/Ag454RrUM4 — Randy Moser (@Randy_Moser_) October 17, 2026 Reyna was everywhere for Strasbourg throughout the match, which represented his first 90-minute performance of the season. He saw 43 touches all over the pitch, with two early shots plus a chance created and a 27-for-32 passing effort. Ultimately, Strasbourg would lose the match 3-1 to the Ligue 1 leaders, who scored three goals in the final 13 minutes of the game. Ilya Zabarnyi found the equalizer in the 77th minute, while substitutes Ousmane Dembele and Desire Doue came off the bench to secure the victory. Gio Reyna stats, goals for Strasbourg The goal was Gio Reyna's second of the season for Strasbourg, as he looks to carve out a regular role in France. He has appeared in all seven of Strasbourg's league matches so far this season, with five of those starts, already more starts than he had all of last season in the Bundesliga with Borussia Monchengladbach. His first goal for the club came in a 6-2 win over Troyes, scoring his team's third in the 57th minute. Reyna has racked up 47 caps for the U.S. national team, scoring 10 goals in his international career.

item.title: Bears Defense Faces Nightmare Against Bijan Robinson
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears defense is heading into a total nightmare for Sunday’s game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. After that 31-7 blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers on October 11, the injury list just keeps growing. It feels like the defensive unit is falling apart right before the Atlanta Falcons arrive. The situation is dire. According to Sports Illustrated , the team lost three vital edge-rushers and linebackers during the past week. Montez Sweat is currently serving a two-game suspension for violating the league’s performance-enhancing substances policy. On top of that, T.J. Edwards is out because he hurt his hamstring during the loss at Lambeau Field. Dayo Odeyingbo is also sidelined with a quadriceps injury, per Sports Illustrated. The Bijan Robinson Problem Losing these guys makes stopping Bijan Robinson nearly impossible. Robinson is a monster lately. He has averaged at least five yards per carry over his last three games while handling at least 17 touches per contest, according to Sports Illustrated. Without the edge-setting of Sweat or the communication from Edwards, the defense is wide open. Even the gravity of Odeyingbo, which often forces double-teams on early downs, will be missing. The Bears defense needs new heroes to show up. Austin Booker had a massive game against Green Bay with two sacks, three tackles for loss, and a forced fumble. He has to do it again to stop Robinson from running to the outside. Finding Depth in the Chaos The depth chart is being tested like never before. Daniel Hardy is a top candidate to see more snaps since Sweat and Odeyingbo are out. Hardy got a multi-year extension in the offseason, and now he has to prove he can handle the edge. James Lynch could also help by providing a big body in the middle of the field. He is a strong run-stopper during his first year in Chicago. There is also some hype around Jamree Kromah. He could get his first regular-season snap this Sunday. During the preseason, Kromah recorded three sacks, four tackles for loss, and a forced fumble. The defensive line is thin, and the team is relying on these unproven pieces to survive the Falcons. The offense might get a boost, but the defense is struggling. Yahoo Sports reported that quarterback Caleb Williams practiced fully all week and is expected to be back in the lineup.

Junior Sherrill deserves more respect as a WR1. He is not as explosive or terrifying on a play-by-play basis as some elite WRs, but he makes plays when called upon. He had his worst game of the year with “just” 5 catches for 55 yards. Still, that accounted for 16% of Vanderbilt’s total offense. He did get some help from another WR in this game. The OL has to sort some issues out. Beyond the penalties, it is so disjointed. They are struggling to identify and pick up blitzes and stunts. I do wonder if some of that is coming from the QB’s inexperience. They are doing a piss poor job in run blocking, too. Averaging 2.8 yards per carry against a defense that, even after that performance, is averaging 4.3 yards per carry against. Between penalties and not consistently moving the ball on the ground, they are making their own lives miserable by getting into 3 rd and longs.Lyndon Cooper is obviously playing injured and is often in and out of the game. Gunner Givens is out today, too, and has been one of the worst culprits on penalties, so it will be interesting to see if his replacement can stake a claim to the job. His punts went 59, 48, 64, and 62 yards. The returns were 11, 13 (plus 5 for an illegal formation), 26 (negated to 13 by a hold), and a bounce-and-bobble fair catch. Averaging 58.3 yards per kick and netting 49.0 yards is how you flip field position. Hampton had the biggest return game gaff, but Dontae Carter also let a kickoff go over his head and bounce straight up at the 2. He had to field it and only returned the ball a few yards. The freshman was 19 of 32 for 222 yards with 1 TD and 2 interceptions while being limited on the ground to just 2 yards from 6 attempts. Both interceptions went off both hands of his intended targets, so neither of them was on him. He was feeling pressure a bit early yet looked hesitant to tuck the ball down. His knee bruise may have influenced that. The tape should provide him with some learning experiences, and nothing was bad enough to think it was going to be a trend. Coming into the game, he was 2 nd in the SEC for air yards per pass attempt at 10.4. He is putting the ball downfield consistently and throws a very catchable, accurate deep ball. The intermediate timing routes are the biggest opportunity for improvement, but the OL needs to give him more chances for rhythm. The pieces besides Sherrill in the passing game may be finding their niches. In a game where the offense really struggled, Ja’Cory Thomas had 3 catches for 60 yards, including a TD. At least two, if not all three, catches were 1v1 sideline throws. He is a problem for a lot of CBs at 6’3 and 215 pounds. Curtis has the ability to put dimes up for him to go get where even if Thomas does not have burner speed to separate, he has the height and vertical to win contested catches, just like the TD where the CB was flagged for DPI. Walter Taylor also had 2 catches for 40 yards with both coming on deep over routes where he got behind LBs and in front of safeties while crossing the field. He presents a big target at 6’7 and has good speed for that height. Cole Spence had a pair of catches for 27 yards, too, even with the drop-turned-interception. In all, 9 players were credited with a reception, and 8 of them caught a pass beyond the LOS. They may not find a great sidekick for Sherrill but having a host of players making small but important plays throughout the game would be nice, too. You could maybe even argue about it being 34 since 1 TD drive was a a single play from 35 yards out. That is likely a FG anyway. Allowing 38 to Ole Miss is not … awful. It would be bang on their average (38.8), which was raised by the 52 points they scored against us. Being average on defense would be … fine. Arkansas’s average for the season is 19.3. Fold or refocus? After a significant loss that felt promising at Georgia, the team played one of their worst games and nuked almost every bit of optimism in the fan base. Clark Lea said they have implemented new in-practice penalties for procedural penalties. That is nice, but I am skeptical it fixes the overarching discipline issues. Today would be a good time to show some intelligence and focus. Is the season sunk, or can a hog roast be a modicum of hope? Arkansas is bad. Bad enough for Vanderbilt to be favored by 5.5 points. That spread has crept down from earlier in the week, which is concerning. Vanderbilt needs to show improvement that can predict future success, not just eek out a win. This is by far the easiest opponent left. Florida has been scuffling but is playing Texas moderately close. Mississippi State is get walloped by LSU, but they have been dangerous plenty often and are without star QB Kamario Taylor. Taylor should be healed by the time the Commodores head to Starkville. item.title: Gianni Infantino reportedly received $1.72 million in undisclosed World Cup compensation
item.description: Source: thenews2.com/Depositphotos FIFA President Gianni Infantino is facing renewed scrutiny after U.S. tax filings reportedly showed that a World Cup-related entity paid him an additional $1.72 million in 2024. The payment was not listed in FIFA’s public compensation disclosure for that year, according to reporting by ESPN. The report has raised questions about how FIFA discloses compensation paid through separate entities. However, the reported omission does not by itself establish that Infantino or FIFA violated any law or organizational rule. FIFA has rejected allegations that it failed to disclose financial information or breached its statutes. The organization says its compensation reporting complies with applicable requirements and that an independent subcommittee determines the president’s annual compensation and other contractual benefits. What the financial filings reportedly show Reporting published on Oct. 13, 2026, said U.S. tax filings showed that FWC2026 US Inc. paid Infantino approximately $1.72 million in 2024. item.title: Iraola hails Fulham players and supporters after first win
item.description: Iraola hails Fulham players and supporters after first win Alvaro Arbeloa hailed Fulham’s character after they secured a 1-0 win over Hull City for their first Premier League victory of the season. The Fulham boss was delighted with the way his side continued to attack after taking the lead through Alex Iwobi and believes the victory was reward for their recent work. “I’m so proud of my players because they played with great personality, great character,” Arbeloa said. “We scored one goal, and we continued attacking in the second half.” Arbeloa was also pleased for the Fulham supporters after seeing his side return to winning ways. “I’m so happy for our supporters – they deserve this victory, this win,” he said. “And for my players.” The Spaniard also praised the squad for continuing to trust in his approach despite pressure building on his position following a poor start. “It’s not easy for players when you are working hard, when you are doing what your coach is asking you, and you don’t win games,” Arbeloa said. “It’s not easy to keep doing the same things, keep working, keep trying to improve. “And my players believe in our ideas, and they play in the way that we are playing, even when we were losing games.”

item.title: Business as usual for victorious Man City despite lingering state of limbo
item.description: Business as usual for Manchester City . Or should that be business as unusual? City may be in a strange kind of limbo but their new normal looked distinctly similar to the old variant. They won. Whatever punishments may await in the wake of the 114 guilty verdicts, which City are appealing, for now they are constructing a title challenge which, perhaps, the Premier League could do without. They are leaders with a six-point advantage at the summit and, some would say, an asterisk or two. But Enzo Maresca ’s stellar start has given him outright possession of a record. The Italian has seven victories out of seven in the top flight, the longest winning start to a reign in the Premier League. Beating Ipswich took him past Carlo Ancelotti, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and his predecessor Pep Guardiola , all tied on six. “For sure I didn’t expect to win seven games out of seven,” said Maresca. “It’s a matter of winning games in this business.” It has been at City, anyway. So life in the wake of the independent commission’s damning conclusions rather resembled the time before it. There was the statutory Erling Haaland goal, as he scored a second successive brace. The Norwegian has 12 goals in his last eight outings for City. A weakened City team had a talisman in attack ensuring that Ipswich’s competitiveness did not earn them a point. item.description: Jaguars make Brian Thomas Jr. decision amid league-wide trade interest originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the NFL trade deadline nears, there is a ton of interest on the Jacksonville Jaguars , but it's not about the 4-1 team being buyers, but rather about if one player is going to be made available. Through the first five weeks of the season, Brian Thomas Jr.'s role in the offense has been minimal at best. With Parker Washington breaking out and Jakobi Meyers signed to an extension, Thomas's name has popped up in trade rumors. However, according to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the Jaguars have made a decision on whether Thomas will be available for trade or not. Unsurprisingly, as of Week 6, Thomas is not on the trade block despite league-wide interest. Jaguars don't put Brian Thomas Jr. on trade block despite interest "After the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, league eyes have turned to Jacksonville Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr.," Jones reports. "... But Jacksonville does not have him on the trade block." While there might be interest from NFL clubs about a trade for Thomas, it appears that the Jaguars are not making him available right now. Washington, Meyers, and Josh Cameron are involved in this Jaguars' passing attack, and Thomas has fallen by the wayside after being taken in the first round in 2024. MORE : Marvin Harrison Jr. vs. Marvin Harrison Sr. stats: How Hall of Fame dad's slow start compares to son in Year 2 But, despite being an obvious trade candidate, the Jaguars are Super Bowl contenders this season, and Jones' report indicates they have no intention of trading Thomas this season. His field-stretching ability and upside as a receiver are enough to justify keeping him on the team, even if his overall involvement in the offense is minimal. He's not on the trade block right now, so fans or NFL teams hoping for their team to improve their WR room might have to look for other WR trade targets this Fall instead of Thomas. item.title: Royals’ $3Bn Downtown Ballpark Wins With Stunning New Renderings
item.description: William Purnell-Imagn Images The Kansas City Royals have finally shown the world what their $3 billion downtown dream looks like, and the reaction is mixed with a sharp edge. Architects released six new images on Thursday that paint a bright picture for the city, yet the real test remains whether ownership will spend enough to win. This is a huge win for the look, but the team must prove it will build a contender, not just a pretty place to sit. Downtown Design Draws Praise The new venue is set to cost about $1.9 billion, with the rest of the funds going toward an 85-acre mixed-use development around it. The Kansas City Council approved plans for a $600 million commitment to support the project, while private investors and the Royals ownership cover the rest. Populous, a local Kansas City firm, designed the stadium that will seat 34,000 fans. Per talkSPORT , the design team was an easy choice for the front office because they wanted the best fan experience in Major League Baseball. Fans are reacting to the new look with a mix of excitement and caution. One fan told talkSPORT, “I wasn’t a fan of moving, but the stadium looks so beautiful. Hope it all comes together like this.” Another added, “This looks absolutely stunning, I just hope management and ownership are going to spend to make them competitive.” The renders show a modern structure that honors the city, but the hope for a winning team hangs in the air. Ownership Must Deliver Wins Royals CEO John Sherman defended the local choice for the architects, noting the firm’s global reputation. “We could have searched the world over for the leading sports architecture firm in the world, but it’s right here in Kansas City,” Sherman said via MLB.com. Construction is set to begin in May 2027, giving the city three years to prepare for the big shift. A third fan told talkSPORT, “I am really excited for the move, they have all looked beautiful, I just hope that they can follow through on what’s been promised.” This sentiment hits the core of the issue for Royals fans who have waited decades for a return to downtown. The building is only half the battle; the team on the field must be ready to play when the gates open. A Test for the City The project represents a massive change for a franchise that has called the Truman Sports Complex home since 1973. A fourth commenter on the new images said, “Its beautiful, a huge win for downtown Kansas City.” A fifth fan concluded, “I love a lot of the details. I can’t wait to enjoy this new stadium! I see so many pieces of History that aren’t being forgotten.” These words show deep pride in the design and the history of the team. Yet the clock is ticking toward the 2030 move, and the pressure is on the owners to back up the beautiful blueprints with a winning roster.

item.title: JJ Jansen Makes NFL History As Panthers Long Snapper Sets Record
item.description: Scott Galvin-Imagn Images History is being made this Sunday, and it is not about touchdowns or interceptions. JJ Jansen will take the field against the Philadelphia Eagles to play his 282nd career game, a number that no other long snapper in NFL history has ever reached. While most fans forget the specialist who snaps the ball between his legs, Jansen has turned a tiny job into a massive legacy. He is not just playing; he is proving that consistency beats flash every single time. Per NBC Sports , this milestone breaks a tie with Trey Junkin, the man Jansen watched as a kid in Arizona. The 40-year-old has spent his entire regular-season career with the Panthers, a rarity in a league where players jump ship for every extra dollar. He started in 2009 after a trade, and he has been the anchor ever since. This is not luck. It is a skill set so rare that only a handful of men in the world can do it at this level. A Father’s Lessons on the Grass Jansen did not learn this craft in a fancy camp or a high-tech facility. He learned it from his dad on a patch of grass in their backyard. The technique required for snapping a football is so precise that a bad snap can cost a team a field goal. Jansen told Darin Gantt of Panthers.com, “I still remember we practiced in the same way every single time,” recalling the hours they spent in front of a tree. He stood at one end, and his dad stood 15 yards away. They had good nights and bad nights, but they kept going. That grind built a player who refuses to quit. Former kicker John Kasay, who held the Panthers’ games played record before Jansen, sees something special in this work ethic. “I think he never got bored with it,” Kasay said. The job is repetitive, but Jansen treats every snap like it matters. He has played 281 games for Carolina alone, and he is still going strong. If he plays every game this season, he will finish with 294 games, placing him 18th on the all-time list for any player. That is a testament to a player who never lost his edge. The Ultimate Specialist Long snappers do not get the glory, but they get the job done. Jansen knows that the only stat that matters for his position is games played. As long as you do not mess up, you keep your spot. He has done that for 17 years. He once joked about watching Junkin warm up on first down, thinking the Cardinals were so bad that the special teams guys had to be ready early. “I always thought it was really funny that the punter and the long snapper would warm up on first down because back then the Cardinals were terrible,” Jansen said. Now, he is the one setting the standard that others will chase for decades. With the next game set for Sunday at 1 p.m. ET against the Eagles, Jansen is ready to add another chapter to his story. He is showing no signs of slowing down, even as he passes the 40-year mark. This is what loyalty looks like in the NFL. He is not just a player; he is a record holder who earned every single one of his snaps. Keep pounding, JJ.

item.title: Celtic Keeper Shaken Again As Per Charlie Mulgrew: Can O’Neill Trust Anyone Between The Sticks?
item.description: Celtic Keeper Shaken Again As Per Charlie Mulgrew: Can O’Neill Trust Anyone Between The Sticks? A 4-1 beating in Lisbon stings. What stung Celtic fans most, though, was how two of those goals arrived. Viljami Sinisalo had only just won the gloves back. Sam Johnstone lost them after a ropey League Cup afternoon at Ibrox, so Martin O’Neill gave the Finn another go. Alexander Bah then made it 2-0 to Benfica, and Sinisalo couldn’t keep it out. Jhon Duran later poked a close-range finish through his legs. Two straight Europa League defeats leave Celtic with a stiff task to reach the knockouts. Charlie Mulgrew didn’t dress it up. Speaking to Premier Sports Ireland, as relayed by Celts Are Here , the former Celtic defender said Sinisalo is “still scratching for a number one”. He added that the 25-year-old keeps failing to make the saves Europe demands. Mulgrew also reckons O’Neill hasn’t found his best XI, and the weak spots keep costing them at this level. Fans can’t really argue. A keeper lives under a microscope, yet the criticism has bite, since every decent side starts at the back. Johnstone could return, though few expect him to change much while question marks hang over defence and midfield. “Sinisalo, for me… still scratching for a number one. “Johnstone’s came in, had a bad time at Ibrox, then came out of the team; Sinisalo back in. “But continually in Europe, for me, Sinisalo doesn’t make the necessary saves.” Can O’Neill settle on a goalkeeper while the defence keeps leaking? GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – JULY 25: Viljami Sinisalo of Celtic arrives at the ground ahead of kick off in the Celtic v AC Milan in a pre-season friendly at Celtic Park on July 25, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by WM Sport Media/Getty Images) From O’Neill’s chair, the gloves aren’t the real itch. Sinisalo gave him two soft ones in one night, but dropping a 25-year-old again could flatten whatever confidence he has left, and Johnstone’s Ibrox wobble leaves no obvious alternative. So O’Neill sticks, probably, and hopes. A keeper can’t save what a back four lets through. Benfica found space far too easily, and O’Neill knows a settled defence protects either goalkeeper better than any swap. He needs to pick his back four, pick his midfield screen, and leave them alone for a month. Constant tinkering is how you end up losing 4-1. Johnstone deserves a go in a domestic game, where a mistake won’t cost a European place. Sinisalo keeps the Thursday nights for now, because chopping and changing sends the loudest message of all: nobody’s sure. A quiet word and a clean sheet against a modest league side could do more for Sinisalo than any team talk. Mulgrew has a point about Europe, mind. Domestic games hide flaws. Europe shows them off.

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

In the Premier League right now, I feel there are a couple of non-negotiables: you’ve got to run more than the other team if you want to win, or at least get close enough that it doesn’t make that much of a difference. item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League.
